## 1. Glitch Origami Hot Drip
Brewer: Origami (Kalita Wave paper). Dose: 14.5g. Total Water Poured: 260g. Yield: 200-210g. Brew Ratio (poured): 1:17.9. Brew Ratio (yield): 1:13.8-14.5. Temperature: 86-90°C (range). Grind: NOT SPECIFIED. Recipe: 30g bloom (0:00-0:05) → 30g (0:20-0:25) → 100g (0:50-1:05) → 100g (1:20-1:35). Target Drawdown: not stated, estimated 2:45-3:00.

Judge's assessment: high-extraction, high-clarity recipe leveraging Origami's fast flow (Kalita wave flat bottom) to push large water volume (260g) through small dose (14.5g). Four-pour pulse structure, aggressive timing (first three pours within 80s), final 100g draws down slowly. ~60g water retained, bed fully saturated. 1:17.9 poured ratio is very dilute — chases transparency/flavour separation at expense of body/sweetness. Wide temp range (86-90°C) signals lack of confidence/precision.

Scores: Sweetness 3/5 (dilute ratio suppresses sugar), Clarity 5/5 (four pulses = exceptional separation), Balance 4/5 (flat-bottom paper reduces channeling), Acidity 4/5 (bright but softened by low temp), Body 2/5 (thin, tea-like — biggest weakness), Complexity 4/5 (layered but dilution mutes mid-palate).

Strengths: excellent clarity, low astringency risk, forgiving of grind inconsistencies, reproducible yield. Limitations: body critically weak, temp range unacceptable for fixed recipe, grind unspecified, dose below specialty standard (15-18g typical), yield-ratio paradox (concentrated by yield but tastes thin due to poured dilution). Recommended fixes: fix temp at 88°C; specify grind (EK43 9.5-10.0 or Comandante 24 clicks); reduce total water to 230g (1:15.9) keeping 200g yield for more retained solids; change pours to 30g bloom → 40g(0:25) → 80g(0:55) → 80g(1:20) to concentrate middle pours; extend bloom to 0:30 for denser beans.

Competition verdict: 6.5/10 — beautiful clarity, too thin/imprecise for finals; workhorse for washed Ethiopian coffees once ratio fixed and temp locked.

## 2. Glitch Origami Iced Drip
Brewer: Origami (Kalita Wave paper). Dose: 14.5g. Total Water Poured: 150g. Yield (coffee): 100-110g. Ice: 80-100g. Total Beverage: ~180-210g. Brew Ratio (hot water:coffee): 1:10.3. Temperature: 86-90°C (range). Grind: NOT SPECIFIED. Recipe: 30g bloom (0:00-0:05) → 20g (0:30-0:35) → 100g (1:00-1:15). Cooling: post-brew, poured over ice.

Judge's assessment: 1:10.3 ratio is highly concentrated to survive ice dilution. Minimalist 3-pour structure: short bloom, tiny 20g second pulse, massive 100g final pour driving bulk of extraction. Rapid post-brew cooling arrests extraction, preserves volatile aromatics. Flat-bottom Origami allows fast flow even with fine grind — crucial for short iced contact time. Wide temp range even more problematic for iced: 86°C risks sour/under-extracted concentrate, 90°C richer but risks bitterness once diluted.

Scores: Sweetness 4/5 (concentration preserves sugars, ice dilution lowers slightly), Clarity 4/5 (holds but dilution/cooling mute high notes), Balance 4/5 (concentrate offsets ice dilution well), Acidity 4/5 (bright but 86°C risks underdevelopment), Body 3/5 (better than hot version — concentrate gives syrupy mouthfeel that survives ice), Complexity 3/5 (cooling flattens nuance, simpler than hot counterpart).

Strengths: excellent concentration strategy/math for tall iced cup, fast efficient brew (~75s pour time), retains clarity despite heavy concentration, low over-extraction risk (cooling stops extraction instantly). Limitations: 20g second pour negligible (barely wets grounds — skip or increase to 40g), temp range disastrous for iced coffee (pick 88°C baseline), grind unspecified (crucial for iced, needs finer grind for short contact), ice amount variable (80-100g changes final TDS significantly — must specify exact weight e.g. 90g), no stirring/swirling specified (fast flow may leave high-and-dry edge grounds). Recommended fixes: fix temp 88°C; specify grind EK43 9.0-9.5 (finer than hot) or Comandante 22 clicks; increase second pour from 20g to 40g at 0:30; fix ice at 90g; extend bloom to 0:10; add gentle swirl at 0:45 after final pour.

Competition verdict: 7.0/10 — best of the four so far (relative to a broader judged set), concentration logic sound, lacks precision (temp/grind/ice) to be podium contender; with adjustments could score 8.5+ in iced brew category.

## 3. Glitch Hario V60 Hot Drip
Brewer: Hario V60 (01 paper). Dose: 15.5g. Total Water Poured: 260g. Yield: 200-210g. Brew Ratio (poured): 1:16.8. Brew Ratio (yield): 1:12.9-13.5. Temperature: 86-90°C (range). Grind: NOT SPECIFIED. Recipe: 60g bloom + stir 5x (0:00-0:10) → 110g (0:30-0:40) → 90g (1:20-1:30). Target Drawdown: not stated, estimated 2:30-2:45.

Judge's assessment: high-agitation, high-extraction recipe built around V60's steep cone geometry. 60g bloom + 5 stirs is aggressive (most recipes use 2-3 stirs or a swirl) — rapidly saturates grounds but risks channeling and fines migration to cone tip, stalling brew. Three-pour "front-loaded" structure: largest pour (110g) at 0:30 drives bulk of extraction early, final 90g acts as rinse. Dose (15.5g) more standard than Origami's 14.5g, better thermal mass. Temp range remains a liability; 5-stir bloom flagged as a consistency risk.

Scores: Sweetness 4/5 (1:16.8 ratio + 15.5g dose improve sugar extraction over Origami), Clarity 3/5 (aggressive stirring clouds cup — fines migration reduces separation), Balance 3/5 (heavy agitation can produce harsh edge if not executed perfectly), Acidity 4/5 (bright/forward especially at 88-90°C), Body 4/5 (better than Origami hot — V60 cone + stirring produce heavier mouthfeel), Complexity 3/5 (stirring homogenises extraction, smooths distinct flavour layers).

Strengths: better mouthfeel/sweetness (V60 spiral ribs + cone geometry), generous bloom accounts for high gas in fresh coffees, simple repeatable three-pour structure, 15.5g dose within optimal thermal mass range. Limitations: 5 stirs excessive (introduces operator variability in speed/depth/angle — more than 3 stirs rarely improves extraction, often degrades clarity), final 90g pour at 1:20 may be too late (bed temp dropped, may under-extract remaining solubles), temp range unacceptable, no grind specification (V60 highly grind-sensitive), high agitation + light roast = high channeling risk especially with forceful pour stream. Recommended fixes: reduce to 3 stirs; fix temp at 89°C; specify grind EK43 9.0-9.5 or Comandante 23 clicks (slightly finer than Origami due to taller bed); move final pour to 1:10 (60g bloom → 110g(0:30) → 90g(1:10)); extend bloom time to 0:15 (3 stirs over 15s more controlled than 5 stirs over 10s); add gentle swirl at 1:15 after final pour to flatten bed.

Competition verdict: 6.0/10 — agitation overdone, lack of precision hurts it, but underlying ratio/dose solid; with adjustments (fewer stirs, fixed temp) could become 7.5-8.0, strong daily driver but not yet finals-worthy.
